title: At my table (2 Samuel 9)
hook: David seeks Jonathan's lame son and seats him at his table always

segments.voice: Yesterday, David danced before the ark in a linen ephod. Your line was with all his might. What did you do full out? Today, the king remembers an old promise. Day seven hundred forty-five.

A question, asked in a palace: is there anyone still left of the house of Saul, so I can show him kindness for Jonathan's sake? David is settled now. He has a city and an army. A new king asking after the old king's family could sound like a threat. But David is remembering a field, and arrows, and an oath Jonathan made him swear: the Lord between me and you, between my children and your children. Someone remembers a name. A servant of Saul's house called Ziba. They send for him.
screen: `IS ANYONE LEFT OF SAUL'S HOUSE?` → `FOR JONATHAN'S SAKE.` → `SEND FOR ZIBA.`

segments.voice: Ziba says yes. There's a son of Jonathan, lame in his feet, living in a place called Lo-debar, in someone else's house. His name is Mephibosheth. Earlier the book tells how it happened: he was a small child when the news came from the battle where his father and grandfather died, and his nurse snatched him up and ran, and he fell. He has lived ever since as the leftover of a fallen house. David sends for him. Mephibosheth comes in and falls on his face. He has every reason to be afraid. David says his name, Mephibosheth, and he answers, here is your servant. Then David tells him, fear not. Then the promise. I will surely show you kindness for Jonathan your father's sake. I will give you back all the land of Saul. And you will eat bread at my table continually. The Hebrew word for kindness here is chesed, loyal love, the faithfulness you owe because of a bond. When David first asked Ziba, he even called it the kindness of God. Mephibosheth can hardly take it in. He calls himself a dead dog. David doesn't argue with him. He just keeps the promise. Ziba and his household are told to work the land for Mephibosheth, and David says he'll eat at the king's table like one of the king's sons. The chapter ends with two facts side by side. Mephibosheth ate always at the king's table. And he was lame in both his feet. Nothing about him had to change to get a seat. The table changed. David kept faith with a friend who was gone by keeping a place for his son.
screen: `A SON OF JONATHAN, LAME IN HIS FEET.` · `FEAR NOT.` · `CHESED: LOYAL LOVE.` · then, large: `ALWAYS AT MY TABLE.` · then: `LIKE ONE OF THE KING'S SONS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: keep faith with a friend's family. Settle, and breathe. Let one friend come to mind who has died, or moved far away, or whom you've simply lost touch with. Now think of the people they left behind: a partner, a child, a parent, a sibling. Someone who might be living, in a small way, in Lo-debar. Ask yourself what a seat at your table would look like for them. A dinner. A message on the anniversary. A story about their person they haven't heard. Choose one. If you pray, you can hold their names. The bell holds the time.
At my table. David's chesed to Jonathan's son: land given back, and a seat at the king's table, always. Today's word.
Your line: always at my table. Today, reach out to someone who belongs to a friend you've lost, and make them a place. Day seven hundred forty-five.

howItsDone: Jews read the story of Mephibosheth in the book of Samuel, part of the Prophets, as an example of chesed, loyal kindness, kept across generations.

fork.setup: you're David, now king. you learn that Jonathan's son is alive, lame, and living in someone else's house. what do you do?
options: leave him alone: he's safer forgotten.
send him money and keep your distance.
bring him in, give back his land, and seat him at your table.
fork.reveal: David says fear not, restores all of Saul's land to him, and seats him at the king's table like one of the king's sons.

original.note: Hebrew: at my table, from David's promise in 2 Samuel 9:7.

trapdoor: what you thought: a king is generous to a disabled man.
what it means: David keeps his oath to Jonathan with chesed, loyal love, and gives his son land and a seat like a king's son.
what a scholar hears: the chapter ends with two facts side by side: always at the king's table, and lame in both his feet.

notes: Whole chapter paraphrased; no quotation marks used.
A general historical claim about kings removing rivals' heirs was cut under the claims rule.
Chesed glossed as loyal love; 'the kindness of God' is 9:3. Confirm.
Mephibosheth's fall is from 2 Samuel 4:4; his age there is left out.
Ziba's later conduct (2 Samuel 16, 19) is left out.
Editor: corrected attribution — in 9:3 it is David, not Ziba, who speaks of 'the kindness of God'; cut the unsourced 'Saul's family has scattered' from the hook.

Audit: the teach and a myth item (marked true) said David's first words to Mephibosheth were 'fear not'; in 9:6–7 David first says his name, Mephibosheth answers 'Behold thy servant', and only then 'Fear not'. Teach and myth corrected.
